cases.doc:
No fresh value from any configured source -- raised only by `assert_available()`; the
usual way to observe this is reading `is_available()`, which returns `false` instead of
panicking. Kept distinct from `ValueDecreased`/`TimestampTooOld`/`DeviationTooHigh`: this
is about the *current* feed state, not about rejecting one submission.
cases.name: OracleUnavailable

cases.doc: A new value (above the current one) moved by more than `max_deviation_bps`. Checked only\nfor increases: a decrease is already rejected first by `ValueDecreased`, so this exists\nspecifically to catch large upward jumps a compromised or malfunctioning feed could push.
cases.name: DeviationTooHigh

cases.doc: `source` does not match the configured primary source, nor the configured fallback (if\nany).
cases.name: InvalidSource

cases.doc: `max_deviation_bps` is zero (would reject every legitimate increase, bricking the feed)\nor above `BPS_SCALE` (100%, a meaningless ceiling).
cases.name: InvalidDeviation

cases.doc: `max_stale_seconds` is zero (would make the feed permanently unavailable).
cases.name: InvalidStaleness

cases.doc: `source` does not match the primary source, and no fallback source is configured at all\n-- so whatever the caller intended, it cannot be a fallback submission either.
cases.name: FallbackNotConfigured

cases.doc: A submitted value fell outside the admin-configured sane range (`set_value_bounds`), if\none has been set. Checked before the deviation guard and even for a value otherwise\nexempt from it (the first-ever submission) -- see `set_value_bounds`'s doc for why.
cases.name: ValueOutOfBounds

cases.doc: `sync_from_feed` called before any `set_feed_source` -- a setup mistake, not routine feed\nnoise, so (unlike everything that feed itself can return) this panics.
cases.name: FeedNotConfigured

udt_union_v0.doc: SEP-40's own asset discriminant (ecosystem/sep-0040.md) -- a feed may quote several assets\nagainst one `base()`, so a pull must say which one.
udt_union_v0.name: Sep40Asset

udt_struct_v0.doc: SEP-40's own return shape, field-for-field: `price` scaled by the feed's own `decimals()`\n(not necessarily this contract's convention -- `sync_from_feed` rescales), `timestamp` in\nUnix seconds.
udt_struct_v0.name: Sep40PriceData

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The most recent `set_reference_value` call this contract refused, if any. `reason` is one of
a small fixed set of short symbols (`decrease`, `stale_ts`, `deviate`, `fb_value`, and, from
`sync_from_feed`, `oob`, `throttle` -- too soon after the last accepted feed update, see
`set_feed_min_interval` -- and `feed_err`, the latter covering both a feed returning an error
and a feed panicking internally, since `try_decimals`/`try_lastprice` surface both the same
way) rather than a free-form string, so a dashboard can map it to display text without
parsing.
udt_struct_v0.name: OracleRejection

function_v0.doc:
Returns true when the stored timestamp is within `max_stale_seconds` of the ledger clock.
Uses `env.ledger().timestamp()` \xe2\x80\x94 callers cannot manipulate this value. Kept as a
caller-supplied-threshold primitive alongside `is_available()`; most callers should prefer
`is_available()` so the threshold lives in one place (this contract's own config) instead
of being duplicated as a constant in every consumer.
function_v0.name: is_fresh

function_v0.doc:
One-time setup. `max_stale_seconds` and `max_deviation_bps` are this feed's own safety
policy (previously a caller-supplied argument to `is_fresh`, now centralized here so every
consumer enforces the same thresholds without duplicating a constant). Sources are not set
here -- call `set_sources` separately, before the first `set_reference_value`.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: The configured SEP-40 feed contract and asset, or `None` if `set_feed_source` has never\nbeen called.
function_v0.name: feed_source

function_v0.doc:
Configure (or reconfigure) the primary and optional fallback source IDs. Each is a
deterministic `BytesN<32>` -- for an off-chain feed, `sha256("principal-oracle-source:
<network>:<asset>:<provider>:<feed>")` (see `docs/ORACLE_SAFETY_EXTENSION.md`); for an
on-chain source, its contract address hash. Passing `fallback_source: None` removes any
existing fallback.
function_v0.name: set_sources

function_v0.doc: `is_fresh` against this contract's own configured `max_stale_seconds`, so a consumer needs\nno threshold of its own. This is this feed's definition of "a usable price is available."
function_v0.name: is_available

function_v0.doc: The configured `(min_value, max_value)` sane range, or `None` if `set_value_bounds` has\nnever been called.
function_v0.name: value_bounds

function_v0.doc: The most recent submission this contract refused by policy (not a malformed call -- see\nthe module doc), or `None` if nothing has ever been rejected.
function_v0.name: last_rejection

function_v0.doc:
Scale this feed's price to `PROTOCOL_DECIMALS`, then run it through this contract's own
freshness/monotonic-value/deviation/sane-bounds policy, exactly as a primary-source
`set_reference_value` submission would -- except every failure here is a graceful
rejection, never a panic (see the module doc for why `sync_from_feed` cannot treat a bad
feed tick the way a malformed admin call is treated). Callable by anyone; there is
nothing to authorize, since it only ever *reads* the configured feed.

Returns `true` if accepted (`Price`/`Timestamp` updated, `last_update_was_feed() == true`
afterward), `false` otherwise -- `last_rejection()` explains why, same as the push path.
function_v0.name: sync_from_feed

function_v0.doc: Single-step admin transfer: current admin authorizes and immediately names a new admin\n(no separate acceptance step from the new admin), matching every other contract's\ntransfer_admin in this codebase.
function_v0.name: transfer_admin

function_v0.doc:
Configure (or reconfigure) which SEP-40-compliant contract `sync_from_feed` pulls from,
and which `Sep40Asset` to ask it for (one feed contract can quote several assets). Fully
independent of `set_sources`/`set_reference_value` above -- both mechanisms can be
configured at once, and whichever last successfully updated `Price`/`Timestamp` wins,
same as primary vs. fallback already works for the push path.
function_v0.name: set_feed_source

function_v0.doc: Panics `OracleUnavailable` unless `is_available()` is true. Gives a caller that wants a\ncrisp revert (rather than reading a boolean and deciding itself) a single cross-contract\ncall to make that happen, propagating this contract's own error code unchanged.
function_v0.name: assert_available

function_v0.doc:
Configure an optional sane absolute range checked against *every* accepted value,
including the first-ever submission (which is otherwise exempt from the deviation guard,
since there is nothing yet to deviate from). Unset by default -- no bound is enforced
until this is called at least once.

This exists to catch an operational mistake the deviation guard cannot: a relay
decimal/scale bug (e.g. submitting an 18-decimal raw amount where the feed expects 8)
that inflates the very first accepted value by many orders of magnitude. Once such a
value were accepted, every subsequent *correct* submission would read as a `decrease`
and be rejected forever -- there is no admin override that can move the stored value
back down, because that would reopen exactly the insolvency path the monotonic-value
invariant exists to close (see the module doc). A sane range catches the bad value before
it is ever stored, which is the only safe place to catch it.
function_v0.name: set_value_bounds

function_v0.doc:
Which configured source (primary or fallback) the currently-stored value last came from.
`None` before the first accepted `set_reference_value`. Only meaningful when
`last_update_was_feed() == false`: a successful `sync_from_feed` updates `Price`/
`Timestamp` but never touches `ActiveSource`, so after it this getter still reports
whichever push-path source last won, not the feed that actually produced the current
value.
function_v0.name: get_active_source

function_v0.doc: Update the feed's own safety thresholds without touching the configured sources.
function_v0.name: set_safety_params

function_v0.doc:
Submit a new value from `source`, which must be the configured primary or fallback.
Returns `true` if accepted (`Price`/`Timestamp`/`ActiveSource` updated), `false` if a
*legitimate* submission was rejected by policy (see the module doc for which outcomes
panic instead). `caller` must match the stored admin and authorize.

The fallback source may only refresh the timestamp of the *current* value (it must submit
exactly the current price); it can never move the value itself. Primary-source updates get
the full monotonic-value and deviation checks.
function_v0.name: set_reference_value

function_v0.doc: Whether the currently-stored `Price`/`Timestamp` came from the last successful\n`sync_from_feed` (`true`) or the last successful `set_reference_value` (`false`).\n`false` before either has ever succeeded.
function_v0.name: last_update_was_feed

function_v0.doc:
Minimum real-time gap, in seconds, between two *accepted* `sync_from_feed` updates.
`0` disables the throttle entirely (intended for tests and tightly-controlled ops, not
for a live market). Admin-only. Does not apply to the admin-only push path
(`set_reference_value`): the throttle exists specifically because `sync_from_feed` is
callable by anyone, for free, at every ledger -- see that function's doc for the bound.
function_v0.name: set_feed_min_interval

function_v0.doc: Effective throttle, i.e. the configured value or\n`DEFAULT_FEED_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS` if `set_feed_min_interval` was never called.
function_v0.name: feed_min_interval_seconds
